steps: A DRAM cell stores a bit as electrical charge on a capacitor.

takeaway: DRAM uses capacitor charge and requires refresh.

optionText.d: Its memory cells consist of flip-flops, and it is used for cache memory.

summary: Processor execution is much faster than main-memory access.
steps: Processor execution is much faster than main-memory access.
Fast cache levels bridge this speed gap by serving frequently used instructions and data. Cache is not a substitute for virtual-memory capacity or a general register.
takeaway: Cache bridges the processor-to-main-memory speed gap.

optionText.a: Cache can be accessed at a high speed, so it is used in the same way as a general-purpose register.
optionText.b: If a cache-miss occurs, the entire cache is erased all at once, and then the latest data is transferred from main memory.
optionText.c: In machines with the large time gap between access to main memory and instruction execution, the effective access time can be shortened by multi-level cache.
optionText.d: When the transfer block size of cache is set to the same size as that of virtual memory, the execution efficiency of a program is enhanced.
